title: Bluegate AutoPay Authorization Terms: Revocation, Card Updates, Changing Method and Reinstatement
content:
**Section A — Who acts.** Only the tenant can revoke or reinstate a Bluegate AutoPay Authorization.

**Section B — Revocation and the next draft.** A revocation stops the next draft only when it is received not later than that due date minus the method's revocation cutoff. Cutoff days are calendar days counted back from the due date, and a revocation on the cutoff day itself is in time. A later revocation takes effect after that due date's draft. A tenant may revoke an authorization that is active, suspended or still pending verification; the authorization then shows cancelled, with the date the revocation is received and the end reason that the tenant revoked it.

*Boundary (hypothetical, 3-day cutoff, next due date the 20th).* The cutoff day is the 17th. A revocation received on the 17th stops the draft for the 20th; one received on the 18th does not, and takes effect after the draft for the 20th.

**Section C — Same-method updates.** A replacement card of the same method, or a new expiry date, is recorded on the existing authorization where the method allows same-method updates, using the last four digits and the expiry exactly as the tenant reads them. Card updates are made only on authorizations in active or suspended status.

**Section D — Changing method.** Moving to a different method, such as from a card to a checking account, needs a new authorization, and the old one is retired when the new one is verified.

**Section E — Reinstatement.** A suspended authorization may be reinstated by the tenant re-authorizing the same method once the cause is fixed, provided reinstatement comes within the method's reinstatement window of the suspension date. Reinstatement days are calendar days counted from the day after the suspension date, and the last counted day is included. A suspension for a closed, lost or stolen card or a closed bank account cannot be reinstated and needs a new method. Reinstatement needs the method's reinstatement requirement, which is the tenant's re-authorization. A reinstated authorization returns to active status.

*Boundary (hypothetical, 30-day window).* Suspended on 1 March: the counted days are 2 March to 31 March. Reinstatement on 31 March is within the window; on 1 April it is not.

**Section F — End of the agreement.** When the covered agreement ends, the authorization is cancelled the same day.

### Status table

| Request | Authorization status in which it can be made |
|---|---|
| Card update (same method) | Active or suspended |
| Reinstatement | Suspended, within the window, cause fixed, and not suspended for a closed, lost or stolen card or a closed bank account |
| Revocation | Active, suspended or pending verification |
